newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania expects 4.0 pct GDP growth by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Romania expects 4.0 pct GDP growth by 2000.

text.p: Romania expects 2.3 percent economic growth in 1998, reversing this year's estimated 3.0 percent downswing in gross domestic product (GDP), the government said on Monday.
It also hopes for a gradual rise in GDP by 2000, with forecast growth of 3.4 percent in 1999 and 4.0 percent in 2000, a document forecasting main indicators to the year 2000 showed.
"The main goal of the (government) economic policy after the 1997-1998 macro-stabilisation period is to ensure a solid recovery," said the document worked out by the Economic Reform Council.
"The (economic) relaunch is expected to bring annual GDP growth rates of above 3.5 percent (in comparable prices) on an average in 1998-2000 interval," it said.
The GDP grew by 4.1 percent last year after a record 7.1 percent rise in 1995.
Romania's new centrist coalition government, which ousted leftists in last November's elections, has embarked on a shock-therapy programme aimed to reshape the economy.
It had already implemented tough monetary and budgetary policies and moved to liberalise fuel, energy and food prices and the foreign exchange markets.
The cabinet also pledged to accelerate privatisation of state companies, restructure inefficient industries and farms and cut the country's bulging current account deficit.
Price liberalisation earlier this year had triggered higher inflation with the monthly rate surging to 30.7 percent in March before slowing to 6.9 percent in April.
The government aims to reduce monthly inflation to about two percent by the end of the year, in line with promises under accords with international lenders.

Lax policies of former leftists in the 1996 election year reignited inflation while bringing large trade and budget deficits. Year-on-year inflation was 56.9 percent last year, up from 27.8 percent in 1995. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
